strings.text: The Lady with the Dog
Gurov has long since ceased to be surprised by anything. Anna Sergeyevna has come to Yalta alone, with a white Pomeranian. Both of them think it will not be for long.
strings.translation: Hace mucho que a Gúrov nada le sorprende. Anna Serguéyevna ha llegado a Yalta sola, con un pomerania blanco. Los dos creen que será cosa de poco tiempo.

strings.text: A holiday romance in Yalta that would not end.
strings.translation: Un romance de veraneo en Yalta que no quiso terminar.

strings.text: after the story by Anton Chekhov
strings.translation: según el relato de Antón Chéjov

strings.text: The sea-front
The dog at his knee
strings.translation: El perrito junto a su rodilla

strings.text: Shake a finger
Pat him
One evening he was dining in the gardens, and she came up and took the next table
strings.translation: Una tarde comía en el jardín, y ella se acercó y se sentó a la mesa de al lado

strings.text: The dog will remember this.
He doesn’t bite
May I give him a bone?
Have you been long in Yalta?
strings.translation: ¿Hace mucho que ha llegado usted a Yalta?

strings.text: Five days
And I have already dragged out a fortnight here
strings.translation: Y yo ya llevo aquí casi dos semanas arrastrándome

strings.text: That’s only the fashion to say it’s dull here. A provincial will live in Belyov and not be dull
strings.translation: Solo es costumbre decir que aquí uno se aburre. Un provinciano vive en Beliov y no se aburre

strings.text: And when he comes here it’s “Oh, the dulness! Oh, the dust!” One would think he came from Grenada
strings.translation: Y cuando llega aquí: «¡Ay, qué aburrimiento! ¡Ay, qué polvo!». Cualquiera diría que viene de Granada

strings.text: The sea was of a soft warm lilac hue, and there was a golden streak from the moon upon it
strings.translation: El agua era de un color lila suave y cálido, y sobre ella la luna tendía una franja dorada

strings.text: He learnt that she was called Anna Sergeyevna, that she was married, and that her husband had a post in S.
strings.translation: Supo que se llamaba Anna Serguéyevna, que estaba casada y que su marido tenía un empleo en S.

strings.text: A week had passed. It was a holiday, a dry wind was blowing, and the steamer came in late
strings.translation: Pasó una semana. Era día de fiesta, soplaba un viento seco, y el vapor llegó tarde

strings.text: She looked through her lorgnette at the passengers, as though looking for acquaintances
strings.translation: Ella miraba a los pasajeros con sus impertinentes, como si buscara a algún conocido

strings.text: Anna Sergeyevna had lost her lorgnette in the crush
strings.translation: Anna Serguéyevna perdió sus impertinentes entre la gente

strings.text: Let us go to your hotel
Oreanda
After the watermelon
Eat at the table
Bring her a slice
The carriage window
Keep looking
Draw the curtain
Her room was close and smelt of the scent she had bought at the Japanese shop
strings.translation: En su habitación hacía bochorno y olía al perfume que había comprado en la tienda japonesa

strings.text: It’s wrong. You will be the first to despise me now
strings.translation: Esto no está bien. Ahora usted será el primero en despreciarme

strings.text: There followed at least half an hour of silence
strings.translation: Pasó por lo menos media hora en silencio

strings.text: It’s not my husband but myself I have deceived
strings.translation: No es a mi marido a quien he engañado, sino a mí misma

strings.text: My husband may be a good, honest man, but he is a flunkey!
strings.translation: Mi marido será quizá un hombre bueno y honrado, ¡pero es un lacayo!

strings.text: I wanted to live! To live, to live…
Hush, hush…
How could I despise you?
At Oreanda they sat on a seat not far from the church, looked down at the sea, and were silent
strings.translation: En Oreanda se sentaron en un banco no lejos de la iglesia, miraban el mar allá abajo y callaban

strings.text: So it must have sounded when there was no Yalta, no Oreanda here; so it sounds now, and it will sound as indifferently and monotonously when we are all no more
strings.translation: Así rumoreaba allá abajo cuando aún no existían ni Yalta ni Oreanda; así rumorea ahora, y seguirá rumoreando igual de indiferente y sordo cuando ya no estemos

strings.text: A man walked up to them — probably a keeper — looked at them and walked away
strings.translation: Se acercó un hombre, probablemente un guarda, los miró y se fue

strings.text: They saw a steamer come from Theodosia, with its lights out in the glow of dawn
strings.translation: Vieron llegar un vapor de Feodosia, iluminado por la aurora, ya con las luces apagadas

strings.text: There is dew on the grass
Yes. It’s time to go home
Every day at twelve o’clock they met on the sea-front, lunched and dined together, went for walks
strings.translation: Cada día a mediodía se encontraban en el paseo marítimo, almorzaban y cenaban juntos, paseaban

strings.text: They kissed in broad daylight, looking round in dread of someone’s seeing them
strings.translation: Se besaban a plena luz del día, mirando alrededor con miedo de que alguien los viera

strings.text: But then a letter came from her husband
strings.translation: Pero entonces llegó una carta del marido

strings.text: Anna, something is wrong with my eyes. Come home, if you can. Don’t overfeed the Pomeranian.
strings.translation: Anna, tengo mal los ojos. Vuelve, si puedes. No sobrealimentes al pomerania.

strings.text: Your husband
Anna, something is wrong with my eyes. Come home, if you can. Don’t overfeed the Pomeranian
strings.translation: Anna, tengo mal los ojos. Vuelve, si puedes. No sobrealimentes al pomerania

strings.text: It’s a good thing I am going away. It’s the finger of destiny
strings.translation: Está bien que me vaya. Es el propio destino

strings.text: Let me look at you once more… Look at you once again. That’s right
strings.translation: Déjeme mirarle una vez más… Mirarle otra vez. Así

strings.text: We are parting for ever — it must be so, for we ought never to have met
strings.translation: Nos despedimos para siempre; así debe ser, porque no deberíamos habernos conocido nunca

strings.text: He was left alone on the platform. The grasshoppers chirruped and the telegraph wires hummed
strings.translation: Se quedó solo en el andén. Cantaban los saltamontes y zumbaban los hilos del telégrafo

strings.text: So that was one more adventure… And it, too, is at an end
strings.translation: Así que una aventura más… Y también ha terminado

strings.text: There was already a scent of autumn at the station; it was a cool evening
strings.translation: En la estación ya olía a otoño; la tarde era fresca

strings.text: Winter
After the sturgeon
Laugh and get into the sledge
Walk away
In Moscow everything was in its winter routine already. The first snow had fallen, and the sledges were out
strings.translation: En Moscú todo era ya invernal. Había caído la primera nieve y salieron los trineos

strings.text: In another month or so it will all be shrouded in a mist in my memory
strings.translation: Pasará un mes, y todo esto quedará envuelto en niebla en mi memoria

strings.text: More than a month passed. She did not visit him in dreams, but followed him about everywhere like a shadow
strings.translation: Pasó más de un mes. Ella no se le aparecía en sueños, sino que lo seguía a todas partes, como una sombra

strings.text: Sometimes at dinner he would suddenly begin talking of love, of women
strings.translation: A veces, en la cena, se ponía de pronto a hablar de amor, de mujeres

strings.text: The part of a lady-killer does not suit you at all, Dimitri
strings.translation: El papel de seductor no te sienta nada bien, Dimitri

strings.text: In S. it was late autumn. Every evening Anna Sergeyevna walked the Pomeranian along the fence
strings.translation: En S. era ya otoño avanzado. Cada tarde Anna Serguéyevna paseaba al pomerania a lo largo de la valla

strings.text: Anna, you’ll catch cold. Come indoors
strings.translation: Anna, te vas a resfriar. Entra en casa

strings.text: One night he was coming out of the doctors’ club with his partner, an official
strings.translation: Una noche salía del club de médicos con su compañero de partida, un funcionario

strings.text: If only you knew what a fascinating woman I made the acquaintance of in Yalta!
strings.translation: ¡Si supiera usted qué mujer tan encantadora conocí en Yalta!

strings.text: Dmitri Dmitritch!
What?
You were right this evening: the sturgeon was a bit too strong!
strings.translation: Tenía usted razón esta tarde: ¡el esturión olía un poco!

strings.text: What savage manners, what people! What senseless nights…
strings.translation: ¡Qué costumbres tan salvajes, qué caras! ¡Qué noches tan absurdas…!

strings.text: He did not sleep all night
strings.translation: No durmió en toda la noche

strings.text: In December, in the Christmas holidays, he made ready for a journey
strings.translation: En diciembre, en las fiestas de Navidad, se preparó para un viaje

strings.text: I am going to Petersburg to do something in the interests of a young friend
strings.translation: Voy a Petersburgo a hacer unas gestiones por un joven amigo

strings.text: Go, Dimitri. Be back by the New Year
strings.translation: Ve, Dimitri. Vuelve para Año Nuevo

strings.text: The town of S.
At the gate
Call the dog
Step round the corner
On the stairs
“I will come to Moscow”
“Go away today”
Her husband at the gate
“To the professor”
“I am going to him”
In S. he took the best room at the hotel. On the table was an inkstand: a figure on horseback, with its hat in its hand and its head broken off
strings.translation: En S. tomó la mejor habitación del hotel. Sobre la mesa había un tintero: un jinete con el sombrero en la mano alzada y la cabeza rota

strings.text: The porter said that von Diderits lived in Old Gontcharny Street, in a house of his own
strings.translation: El portero le dijo que Von Dideritz vivía en la calle Stáraya Goncharnaya, en casa propia

strings.text: One would run away from a fence like that
strings.translation: De una valla así cualquiera huiría

strings.text: He heard a piano; the sounds were faint and indistinct. Probably it was Anna Sergeyevna playing
strings.translation: Oyó un piano; los sonidos eran débiles, confusos. Seguramente tocaba Anna Serguéyevna

strings.text: The maid will remember this.
He wanted to call to the dog — and could not remember its name
strings.translation: Quiso llamar al perro, y no pudo recordar cómo se llamaba

strings.text: On the fence hung a poster: that evening “The Geisha” was to be given at the theatre for the first time
strings.translation: En la valla colgaba un cartel: esa noche se estrenaba en el teatro «La geisha»

strings.text: So much for the lady with the dog… So much for the adventure… You’re in a nice fix…
strings.translation: Pues vaya con la dama del perrito… Vaya aventura… Ahora quédate aquí sentado…

strings.text: She was lost in the provincial crowd, this little woman with a vulgar lorgnette in her hand
strings.translation: Se perdía entre el gentío provinciano, esta mujercita con unos impertinentes vulgares en la mano

strings.text: A young man with small side-whiskers, very tall and stooping, came in with her. He bowed at every step
strings.translation: Con ella entró un joven de patillas cortas, muy alto y encorvado. Hacía una reverencia a cada paso

strings.text: This was the husband whom at Yalta she had called a flunkey
strings.translation: Era el marido al que ella, en Yalta, había llamado lacayo

strings.text: Good evening
How you have frightened me! Why have you come? Why?
strings.translation: ¡Qué susto me ha dado! ¿Por qué ha venido? ¿Por qué?

strings.text: But do understand, Anna, do understand…
I will come and see you in Moscow. I swear I’ll come. But now let us part!
strings.translation: Iré a verle a Moscú. Le juro que iré. ¡Pero ahora separémonos!

strings.text: My precious, good one, let us part!
Go away today. I have never been happy, and I never shall be. Don’t make me suffer still more!
strings.translation: Váyase hoy mismo. Nunca he sido feliz y nunca lo seré. ¡No me haga sufrir todavía más!

strings.text: She held out till the spring
A month later she made ready to go to Moscow
strings.translation: Un mes después se preparó para ir a Moscú

strings.text: When will you be back?
In a week. The professor told me to come again
strings.translation: Dentro de una semana. El profesor me dijo que volviera

strings.text: That’s for the professor. And buy yourself something in Moscow
strings.translation: Esto es para el profesor. Y cómprate algo en Moscú

strings.text: Her husband believed her, and did not believe her
strings.translation: Su marido la creía y no la creía

strings.text: Von Diderits will remember this.
I am going to him
I knew
Go. Only the town must not know. The Pomeranian stays with me
strings.translation: Ve. Solo que en la ciudad no se sepa. El pomerania se queda conmigo

strings.text: Two lives
His wife in the doorway
“At the club”
“I was with her”
She came to Moscow once in two or three months. He came home late from her
strings.translation: Ella venía a Moscú una vez cada dos o tres meses. Él volvía tarde de verla

strings.text: Where have you been, Dimitri?
At the club. We played till two
strings.translation: En el club. Jugamos hasta las dos

strings.text: His wife will remember this.
I was with her
Hush. The children are asleep
On another of her visits, in the morning, he was taking his daughter to school
strings.translation: En otra de sus visitas, por la mañana, él llevaba a su hija al colegio

strings.text: It’s three degrees above freezing, and yet it is snowing
strings.translation: Hace tres grados sobre cero, y sin embargo nieva

strings.text: The thaw is only on the surface of the earth; there is quite a different temperature at a greater height in the atmosphere
strings.translation: El calor está solo en la superficie de la tierra; en las capas altas de la atmósfera la temperatura es muy distinta

strings.text: And why are there no thunderstorms in the winter, father?
strings.translation: Papá, ¿y por qué en invierno no hay truenos?

strings.text: He explained that, too
He had two lives: one open, full of relative truth and of relative falsehood, and another life running its course in secret
strings.translation: Tenía dos vidas: una a la vista, llena de verdad relativa y de engaño relativo, y otra que transcurría en secreto

strings.text: All personal life rests on secrecy
strings.translation: Toda vida personal descansa en el secreto

strings.text: A man in a red cap brought him a note
strings.translation: Un hombre con gorra roja le trajo una nota

strings.text: I have come. The Slaviansky Bazaar.
A.
I have come. The Slaviansky Bazaar
Don’t cry, my darling…
His hair was already beginning to turn grey
strings.translation: Su cabello ya empezaba a encanecer

strings.text: She was wearing his favourite grey dress
strings.translation: Ella llevaba su vestido gris, el que más le gustaba a él

strings.text: They were like a pair of birds of passage, male and female, caught and forced to live in different cages
strings.translation: Eran como dos aves de paso, macho y hembra, a las que hubieran atrapado y obligado a vivir en jaulas separadas

strings.text: How can we be free from this intolerable bondage?
My wife knows
And what now?
My husband knows. He let me go — and kept the Pomeranian
strings.translation: Mi marido lo sabe. Me dejó ir, y se quedó con el pomerania

strings.text: And what now?
Move to Moscow
And he? He is not to blame for anything
strings.translation: ¿Y él? Él no tiene la culpa de nada

strings.text: If only we could go away together…
And the children?
If only we could see each other every day…
And say goodbye every day?
How? How?

And it seemed as though in a little while the solution would be found, and then a new and splendid life would begin; and it was clear to both of them that they had still a long, long road before them, and that the most complicated and difficult part of it was only just beginning
strings.translation: Y parecía que un poco más y la solución sería encontrada, y entonces empezaría una vida nueva y hermosa; y los dos veían claro que el final estaba todavía lejos, muy lejos, y que lo más complicado y difícil no había hecho más que empezar

strings.text: Three windows
A new face
Call to him
It was said that a new person had appeared on the sea-front: a lady with a little dog
strings.translation: Se decía que en el paseo marítimo había aparecido una cara nueva: una dama con un perrito

strings.text: Dmitri Dmitritch Gurov, who had by then been a fortnight at Yalta, had begun, too, to take an interest in new arrivals
strings.translation: Dmitri Dmítrich Gúrov, que llevaba ya dos semanas en Yalta, también había empezado a interesarse por las caras nuevas

strings.text: He almost always spoke ill of women, and called them “the lower race”
strings.translation: De las mujeres hablaba casi siempre mal, y las llamaba «raza inferior»

strings.text: Touch the dog
Go on
Play again
Play the chapter again
Ending
Her hand lay on the bedspread, palm down
strings.translation: Su mano descansaba sobre la colcha, con la palma hacia abajo

strings.text: From the house came the sounds of a piano, faint and indistinct
strings.translation: De la casa llegaban los sonidos de un piano, débiles, confusos

strings.text: Wet snow was falling; his daughter held his hand
strings.translation: Caía aguanieve; su hija le daba la mano

strings.text: The Pomeranian looked at the stranger’s hand and did not dare come near
strings.translation: El pomerania miraba la mano del desconocido y no se atrevía a acercarse

strings.text: Live in one town
Go away together
See each other every day
Then they spent a long while taking counsel together
Her?
The audience came in and took their seats
strings.translation: El público entraba y tomaba asiento

strings.text: The Pomeranian pulled to the end of the fence, toward the station road
strings.translation: El pomerania tiraba hacia el final de la valla, hacia el camino de la estación

strings.text: People walked in the avenue, and anyone might look round
strings.translation: Por la alameda paseaba gente, y cualquiera podía volverse a mirar

strings.text: Passengers came down the gangway; there might be acquaintances among them
strings.translation: Los pasajeros bajaban por la pasarela; entre ellos podía haber conocidos

strings.text: Below, the sea murmured, and it was growing light
strings.translation: Abajo rumoreaba el mar, y amanecía

strings.text: Women passed in the street, and from far off each one looked like her
strings.translation: Por la calle pasaban mujeres, y de lejos cada una se parecía a ella

strings.text: The samovar was hot, and she was still crying at the window
strings.translation: El samovar estaba caliente, y ella seguía llorando junto a la ventana

strings.text: There was a watermelon on the table
strings.translation: Sobre la mesa había una sandía

strings.translation: El reloj está abierto cuando Gúrov no oculta nada, cerrado cuando se lo toma todo a la ligera.

The leash is longer when Anna lets herself live, shorter when she remembers her duty.
strings.translation: La correa es más larga cuando Anna se permite vivir, más corta cuando recuerda su deber.
